# s10 — Turn \newpage and \pagebreak into page breaks

Pandoc parses `\newpage`, `\pagebreak`, and `\clearpage` as raw TeX, and the
HTML writer drops raw TeX, so a page break written for branded-pdf silently
disappears.

**Findings:** G5 · **Size:** S · **Tree:** core

**Not in this slice:** translating any other LaTeX command.

## Why

These are the commands Markdown written for a LaTeX pipeline uses to control
pagination. Other raw TeX is also dropped without notice today.

## Files

- `quire.py` (`render`, after the AST is parsed)
- `test_render.py`
- `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

## Failing tests

- A raw TeX block `\newpage`, `\pagebreak`, or `\clearpage` becomes an empty
  `<div class="quire-page-break">` in the HTML.
- The same command as raw inline TeX inside a paragraph is converted too.
- Any other raw TeX block or inline is dropped with one stderr warning per
  build naming the source file and the first command.
- The page-break rule is present with `--no-css`.

## Implement

Walk the parsed Pandoc AST in `render` and replace matching `RawBlock`/
`RawInline` nodes in the `tex` or `latex` format with raw HTML. Inject
`.quire-page-break { break-after: page; page-break-after: always; }` alongside
the existing diagram safety style so it applies with any stylesheet,
including none. Warn once per build about other raw TeX.

## Check

- `python3 test_quire.py`
- Real build of a three-paragraph document with `\newpage` between them;
  report the page count.
